K1.name: Higashiyama walk at 7:00
K1.desc: Kiyomizu-dera, Sannenzaka, Yasaka Pagoda, Ishibei-kōji, Kōdai-ji (K1a–K1e)
K1.why: Kyoto's most beautiful old streets, nearly empty at 7:00. By 10:00 the same lanes are shoulder to shoulder.
K1.hours: Kiyomizu-dera from 6:00; lanes 24 h (shops from ~9:00–10:00); Kōdai-ji from 9:00.
K1.access: From HOTEL TAVINOS walk ~25 min up Gojō-zaka and Chawan-zaka, or taxi ~10 min to the Kiyomizu-dera gate.
see: K1a Kiyomizu-dera: the wooden stage and the Otowa waterfall.
K1b Sannenzaka and Ninenzaka: stone steps between wooden shopfronts.
K1c Yasaka Pagoda from the top of Yasaka-dōri.
K1d Ishibei-kōji: the quiet stone-walled lane.
K1e Kōdai-ji: Nene's temple, garden and bamboo grove.

route.enter: Kiyomizu-dera main gate (Niō-mon) at the top of Kiyomizu-zaka, ~7:00.
walk: Kiyomizu-dera loop, exit by the same gate (7:00–8:00).
Down Kiyomizu-zaka, right into Sannenzaka steps, then Ninenzaka.
Left up Yasaka-dōri for the pagoda photo, back down.
Nene-no-michi north; Ishibei-kōji on the left.
Kōdai-ji on the right side of Nene-no-michi (~9:15).
route.exit: From Kōdai-ji walk ~10 min to Higashiyama Stn (Tōzai Line) for Keage and Nanzen-ji.

facts: The whole walk is about 2.5 km, mostly downhill once you leave Kiyomizu-dera.
This hill area survived the WWII air raids and the 1950s rebuilding, so the wooden streets are mostly Meiji and Taishō era.
tips: Wear shoes with grip: the stone steps are steep and can be wet.
Konbini breakfast before 7:00; cafés open around 9:00.

K1a.name: Kiyomizu-dera
K1a.desc: Wooden stage over the hillside, Otowa waterfall
K1a.why: Opens at 6:00, so we see it just after sunrise before the tour groups arrive.
K1a.hours: 6:00–18:00 daily. Autumn night opening 21–30 Nov (after we leave Kyoto).
K1a.access: From the hotel ~25 min on foot uphill via Gojō-zaka, or taxi ~10 min.
see: Hondō main hall and its wooden stage, 13 m above the slope.
The view back to the stage from the Okuno-in hall: the classic photo.
Otowa waterfall: three streams under the stage.
Three-storey pagoda (Sanjūnotō), red and gold, by the entrance.
Zuigu-dō (Tainai-meguri), a pitch-dark walk; may open later than 7:00.

route.enter: Niō-mon gate, then the ticket booth before the Hondō.
walk: Hondō and the stage.
Continue to Okuno-in for the side view of the stage.
Steps down to the Otowa waterfall.
Back up the slope path to the gate.
route.exit: Niō-mon gate, then down Kiyomizu-zaka to Sannenzaka (K1b).

facts: Founded in 778; the present main hall was rebuilt in 1633 by order of the third Tokugawa shogun, Iemitsu.
The stage stands on 18 zelkova pillars and is built without nails.
The Otowa streams are said to give long life, success in love and success in study: drink from only one, since taking all three is greedy.
Jishu Shrine (the love stones) is under restoration: it may be closed.
tips: The 📿 stamp desk may not be open at 7:00; try again on the way out.
Bring coins for the waterfall cups area and the ticket.

K1b.name: Sannenzaka and Ninenzaka
K1b.why: The classic old Higashiyama streets, almost empty before 9:00.
K1b.access: Directly below Kiyomizu-dera: turn right off Kiyomizu-zaka at the stone steps.
see: The stone steps of Sannenzaka.
Ninenzaka's row of wooden machiya.
Starbucks Ninenzaka Yasaka Chaya: a 100-year-old townhouse with tatami rooms upstairs (opens 8:00, verify).
Hyōtan (gourd) shop at the bottom of Sannenzaka: gourds are sold as charms against falls.

route.enter: Top of Sannenzaka, from Kiyomizu-zaka.
walk: Down Sannenzaka's steps.
Bend left into Ninenzaka.
At the end, turn left for Yasaka-dōri and the pagoda (K1c).
route.exit: Ninenzaka north end → Nene-no-michi.

facts: The name may come from the third year of the Daidō era (808), when the slope was laid, or from 'Sannei-zaka', the slope of safe childbirth leading to a temple of Kannon for mothers.
The painter-poet Takehisa Yumeji lived on Ninenzaka in 1917.
tips: Photos without people: be here before 8:30.
Watch your step: trivia says falling here brings bad luck.

K1c.name: Yasaka Pagoda (Hōkan-ji)
K1c.why: The best photo of old Kyoto, seen from the lane.
K1c.hours: Outside view 24 h. Interior opens irregularly (~10:00–15:00, verify on the day).
see: The view up Yasaka-dōri with the pagoda at the end.
The corner of Yasaka-dōri and Ninenzaka for the side view.

route.enter: Walk up Yasaka-dōri from Ninenzaka.
walk: Photo from the slope below the pagoda.
Back down the same way.
route.exit: Return to Ninenzaka / Nene-no-michi.

facts: The pagoda is about 46 m tall; the present one dates from 1440, rebuilt by the shogun Ashikaga Yoshinori.
Hōkan-ji is a branch temple of Kennin-ji (K3).
tips: Stand back from the road: residents' cars use the lane.

K1d.name: Ishibei-kōji
K1d.desc: Quiet stone-walled alley with old inns
K1d.why: A calm side lane, a good place to leave the crowds.
K1d.access: Entrance off Nene-no-michi, opposite the Kōdai-ji approach; a second entrance from Shimogawara-dōri.
see: Paved lane between high stone walls (ishibei).
Old ryokan and restaurant gates.

route.enter: From Nene-no-michi, the narrow opening on the west side.
walk: The lane makes a dog-leg; follow it to Shimogawara-dōri.
route.exit: Back to Nene-no-michi and up the steps to Kōdai-ji.

facts: The lane was laid out in the Taishō era (1912–1926) as a private road of rental houses for geiko and rich merchants.
tips: Residential: keep voices low, no tripods, don't block inn gates.

K1e.name: Kōdai-ji
K1e.desc: Zen temple of Nene, wife of Hideyoshi; garden and bamboo grove
K1e.why: A samurai-era temple with a beautiful garden, open from 9:00, the end point of the morning walk.
K1e.hours: 9:00–17:30, last entry 17:00. Autumn night illumination 23 Oct–13 Dec, to 22:00 (last entry 21:30).
K1e.price: ¥600 (includes the Shō museum across the street).
K1e.access: Steps up from Nene-no-michi; 7 min from bus stop Higashiyama Yasui.
see: Kaisan-dō and its pond garden attributed to Kobori Enshū.
The covered 'dragon corridor' climbing to the Otamaya.
Otamaya: Hideyoshi and Nene's mausoleum, with gold makie lacquer ('Kōdai-ji makie').
Two teahouses on the hill, Kasa-tei and Shigure-tei, attributed to Sen no Rikyū.
A small bamboo grove on the way out.

route.enter: Main gate at the top of the steps from Nene-no-michi.
walk: Hōjō and its dry garden.
Kaisan-dō and the pond.
Corridor up to the Otamaya.
Teahouses, then down through the bamboo.
route.exit: Exit gate by the bamboo, back to Nene-no-michi; Higashiyama Stn ~10 min.

facts: Founded in 1606 by Nene (Kita no Mandokoro) in memory of Hideyoshi.
Tokugawa Ieyasu paid for much of the building, to keep Hideyoshi's widow on his side.
tips: Shoes off in the halls: socks.

K2.name: Gion and Shirakawa evening
K2.desc: Geiko district, canal and lanterns (K2a–K2c); booked night walk
K2.why: Wooden teahouses and the canal at lantern time, explained by local students.
K2.price: Tour €39.64 for both (paid). Yasaka Shrine free.
K2.access: Meet 17:50 at the Minamiza Theater entrance, east end of Shijō-Ōhashi bridge. From the hotel ~20 min walk or Keihan Kiyomizu-Gojō → Gion-Shijō (1 stop).
K2.booking: BOOKED: Gion & Geisha Night Walk with Local Students, Tue 17 Nov 18:00 (GetYourGuide GYG996QHG68N).
see: Minamiza, Kyoto's kabuki theatre (meeting point).
K2a Shirakawa canal and Tatsumi Bridge.
Yasaka Shrine, lit at night.
Ryōzen Kannon, Ninenzaka, Hōkan-ji and Yasui Kompira-gū (on the tour route).
K2b Hanamikoji-dōri and K2c Ichiriki-tei.

route.enter: Minamiza entrance, 17:50.
walk: The route is the guide's: Shirakawa, Tatsumi shrine, Yasaka Shrine, Ryōzen Kannon, Ninenzaka, Hōkan-ji, Yasui Kompira-gū, Hanamikoji.
route.exit: Ends ~20:00 around Hanamikoji; Pontochō (K11) is ~10 min west across the river.

facts: Gion grew in the 1600s as a tea-house town for pilgrims to Yasaka Shrine.
In Kyoto they say geiko, not geisha.
tips: No photos of maiko or geiko without asking; never touch or follow them.
Private alleys are signed: photos there can bring a ¥10,000 fine.

K2a.name: Shirakawa canal and Tatsumi Bridge
K2a.why: The most photogenic corner of Gion, lit at dusk.
K2a.access: 5 min north of Shijō-dōri along Hanami-kōji's north part; on the booked night walk.
see: Tatsumi-bashi, the small bridge over the canal.
Tatsumi Daimyōjin, the tiny shrine at the bridge, visited by geiko and maiko.
Shinbashi-dōri: stone-paved, with ochaya houses on both sides.

route.enter: With the guide from Minamiza.
walk: Along the canal, bridge, shrine, Shinbashi-dōri.
route.exit: On to Yasaka Shrine with the tour.

facts: Tatsumi means south-east, the direction the shrine protects.
Shinbashi is a preserved historic district, so the houses keep their wooden fronts by law.
tips: Good for photos even in the dark: lanterns light the canal.

K2b.name: Hanamikoji-dōri
K2b.desc: Main geiko street lined with ochaya teahouses
K2b.why: The classic Gion street; geiko often walk to appointments at dusk (typical, not guaranteed).
K2b.access: South from Shijō-dōri at Ichiriki-tei; on the booked night walk.
see: Wooden façades with bamboo blinds (sudare) and lanterns.
Gion Kōbu Kaburenjō theatre at the south end.
Kennin-ji's north gate at the very end (K3).

route.enter: From Shijō-dōri at Ichiriki-tei.
walk: South along the main street; side lanes are private.
route.exit: Back to Shijō-dōri.

facts: Name tags (ita) by the doors list the maiko and geiko of each house.
tips: Stay in the main street; the side lanes carry 'no photos' signs.

K2c.name: Ichiriki-tei
K2c.desc: Famous red-walled ochaya; outside view only
K2c.why: The best-known teahouse in Gion, seen from the street at the corner of Hanamikoji.
see: The red bengara walls and the noren curtain with the 一力 sign.

route.enter: Street corner.
walk: View from across the street.
route.exit: On along Hanamikoji.

facts: Over 300 years old. The name 一力 is the character 万 (Man-ya, its old name) split in two.
Ōishi Kuranosuke, leader of the 47 rōnin, partied here to make his enemies believe he had given up revenge.
tips: Don't stand in the doorway: guests arrive by taxi.

K3.name: Kennin-ji
K3.desc: Kyoto's oldest Zen temple, twin-dragon ceiling
K3.why: Quiet Zen gardens right in Gion, rarely crowded.
K3.hours: Nov–Feb 10:00–16:30, last entry 16:00. Closed 28–31 Dec and on some memorial days.
K3.access: South end of Hanamikoji; ~10 min from Gion-Shijō Stn (Keihan); ~15 min walk from the hotel.
see: Hattō hall ceiling: Twin Dragons (Sōryū-zu), painted in 2002.
Fūjin and Raijin (Wind and Thunder Gods) screens: a high-quality copy of Tawaraya Sōtatsu's National Treasure.
Chōon-tei courtyard garden.
○△□ garden (circle, triangle, square).
Daiō-en dry garden in front of the Hōjō.

route.enter: Ticket entrance at the Honbō (main residence), north side.
walk: Hōjō and gardens (shoes off, follow the corridor).
Out and across to the Hattō for the dragons.
route.exit: North gate onto Hanamikoji, or west gate; taxi to Shōgunzuka from Yamato-ōji-dōri.

facts: Founded in 1202 by the monk Eisai (Yōsai).
Eisai brought tea seeds from China and wrote Japan's first book on tea, so Kennin-ji is seen as a birthplace of Japanese tea culture.
The twin dragons cover 108 tatami mats and mark the temple's 800th anniversary.
tips: Photos are allowed in most rooms (not of the original screens, which are in the Kyoto National Museum).
📿 stamp at the reception.

K4.name: Nijō Castle
K4.why: Ieyasu's own Kyoto palace with original painted rooms; the key Shōgun site in Kyoto.
K4.hours: 8:45–17:00, last entry 16:00 (Ninomaru Palace 16:10). Honmaru Palace closed the 3rd Monday of the month and the next day (16–17 Nov).
K4.price: Included in the tour (castle + Ninomaru ¥1,300 if bought separately).
K4.access: Tōzai Line Nijōjō-mae Stn, 1 min to the east gate. From Saga-Arashiyama: JR Sagano Line to Nijō (~15 min), then ~10 min walk.
K4.booking: BOOKED: Samurai Walking Tour (Trip Tomo), Sun 15 Nov 13:00–16:00, admission included (GetYourGuide GYG6H7ZV6QYX).
see: Higashi-Ōte-mon, the east gate.
Kara-mon gate, gold and carved.
Ninomaru Palace: 33 rooms, Kano-school painted doors, nightingale floors.
Ōhiroma, the great audience hall.
Ninomaru garden, attributed to Kobori Enshū.
Honmaru: walls, moat and keep base (view over the castle).

route.enter: Higashi-Ōte-mon (east gate), 12:50, meet the TripTomo sign. Don't buy tickets first.
walk: The guide's route: Kara-mon → Ninomaru Palace → garden → Honmaru moat and keep base.
route.exit: Back at the east gate; Nijōjō-mae Stn 1 min.

facts: Built from 1601 to 1603 by Tokugawa Ieyasu as his residence when visiting the emperor's capital.
In 1867, in the Ōhiroma, the last shogun Tokugawa Yoshinobu announced the return of power to the emperor: the shogunate began and ended in this castle.
2026 is the 400th anniversary of Emperor Go-Mizunoo's visit in 1626.
tips: Shoes off in the palace: thick socks, the floors are cold.
No photos inside the palace.

K5.name: Arashiyama at 7:00
K5.why: Bamboo grove, moss garden and a hilltop villa garden before the crowds.
K5.hours: Bamboo grove 24 h. Ōkōchi Sansō 9:00–17:00 (last entry 16:30). Giō-ji 9:00–17:00 (last entry 16:30).
K5.price: Grove free. Ōkōchi ¥1,000 (matcha and sweet included). Giō-ji ¥300.
K5.access: JR Kyoto → Saga-Arashiyama 15 min (¥240), then ~10 min walk to the grove. Leave the hotel ~6:15.
see: The bamboo path (Chikurin no Komichi) at 7:00.
Tenryū-ji garden (K14) from 7:30.
Ōkōchi Sansō villa garden, view over Kyoto to Mt. Hiei.
Giō-ji moss garden, 20 min walk north.

route.enter: Use the Bamboo Forest pin (not the Togetsukyō pin): from Saga-Arashiyama Stn walk west via Nonomiya Shrine.
walk: Bamboo path 7:00–7:30.
Tenryū-ji north gate 7:30–8:30.
Optional K25/K26 8:30–9:00.
Ōkōchi Sansō 9:00–10:15 (top of the bamboo path).
North through Ogura-yama lanes to Giō-ji ~10:20–10:50.
route.exit: Back to JR Saga-Arashiyama (~20 min walk), train to Nijō ~12:15.

facts: Arashiyama was a country retreat for Heian aristocrats more than 1,000 years ago.
The Ministry of the Environment lists the sound of the bamboo among Japan's 100 soundscapes to preserve.
tips: Main street (Saga-Arashiyama shopping street) gets crowded from 10:00: avoid it.
📿 stamp at Giō-ji.

K7.name: Fushimi Inari Taisha
K7.desc: Torii tunnels up a forested mountain at dawn
K7.why: Torii tunnels up a forested mountain; before 8:00 is the quiet window.
K7.hours: Grounds 24 h, free. Shrine office (📿 stamp) ~8:30–16:30 (verify).
K7.access: Keihan Kiyomizu-Gojō 5:49 → Fushimi-Inari 5:56 (¥240), 5 min walk. Back: JR Inari Stn, opposite the main gate.
see: Rōmon gate and the main hall (1499).
Senbon Torii: the double tunnel of torii.
Okusha and the Omokaru stones (lift one and guess its weight to test a wish).
Yotsutsuji crossroads: view over south Kyoto at sunrise.

route.enter: Main torii opposite JR Inari Stn, then Rōmon gate.
walk: Main hall → Senbon Torii → Okusha (~15 min).
Climb to Yotsutsuji (40–50 min from the gate).
A little beyond if time allows; the full summit loop (2–3 h) does not fit.
Back down the same path.
route.exit: Main gate → JR Inari Stn, 8:33 train to Uji.

facts: Founded in 711; head shrine of about 30,000 Inari shrines in Japan.
There are about 10,000 torii; each is donated by a person or company, with the name and date on the back.
The foxes are Inari's messengers; many hold a key to the rice granary in their mouth.
tips: Sunrise ~6:15: the first torii are dark; a phone torch helps.
Toilets at the main gate and at Yotsutsuji.

K8.name: East route
K8.why: Temples, a brick aqueduct and a canal path; a calm half day.
K8.access: Tōzai Line Higashiyama → Keage (~5 min), then ~10 min walk via the Nejiri-mampo tunnel.
see: K8a Nanzen-ji with the aqueduct and Sanmon gate.
Yudōfu lunch near Nanzen-ji.
Optional K20 Eikan-dō.
K8b Philosopher's Path north to Ginkaku-ji.
K8c Ginkaku-ji garden loop.

route.enter: Keage Stn exit 1, through the brick tunnel under the incline railway.
walk: Philosopher's Path 14:30–15:15.
Ginkaku-ji 15:15–16:15.
route.exit: Ginkaku-ji → bus 5/17/203 from Ginkakuji-michi, or taxi back (~20 min).

facts: The whole route is about 4 km on foot.
tips: Flat and easy after the morning hills; a good 'medium' afternoon.

K8a.name: Nanzen-ji
K8a.desc: Zen temple with the brick aqueduct and Sanmon gate
K8a.why: A large, calm temple with a famous brick aqueduct inside the grounds.
K8a.hours: Mar–Nov 8:40–17:00 (Nov weekends and holidays to 17:15); last entry 20 min before closing. Closed 28–31 Dec.
K8a.price: Grounds and aqueduct free. Hōjō garden ¥600, Sanmon gate ¥600. Nanzen-in special opening in Nov 2026, ¥500.
see: Sanmon gate: climb to the balcony for the view over Kyoto.
Hōjō: 'Leaping tiger' dry garden attributed to Kobori Enshū, and Kano Tanyū's tiger paintings.
Suirokaku: red-brick aqueduct (1890) still carrying canal water.
Optional Nanzen-in, behind the aqueduct (special opening in November).

route.enter: Chokushi-mon / main approach from the west (from Keage).
walk: Sanmon gate (climb).
Hattō (outside).
Hōjō garden.
Right behind the Hōjō: Suirokaku aqueduct; walk up the steps to the canal on top.
route.exit: Back to the main approach for the yudōfu shops (Okutan, Junsei).

facts: Founded in 1291 by the retired emperor Kameyama in his villa.
The Sanmon (1628) was donated by the daimyō Tōdō Takatora for the soldiers who died at the siege of Osaka Castle.
In kabuki, the thief Ishikawa Goemon stands on this gate and cries 'Zekkei kana!' ('What a view!').
tips: Yudōfu (simmered tofu) is the classic lunch here; Okutan's garden restaurant is the old one (cash, verify hours).

K8b.name: Philosopher's Path
K8b.desc: 2 km canal walk lined with cherry trees
K8b.why: A quiet canal walk between Nanzen-ji and Ginkaku-ji.
K8b.access: South end at Nyakuōji-bashi (near Eikan-dō); north end at Ginkaku-ji-bashi.
see: Canal with stone bridges to private houses.
Hōnen-in, a moss-roofed gate just off the path (free grounds).
Ōtoyo Shrine with guardian mice instead of lions.
Small cafés and craft shops.

route.enter: South end, Nyakuōji-bashi bridge.
walk: North along the canal (west bank is quieter).
route.exit: North end at Ginkaku-ji-bashi, turn right up the slope to Ginkaku-ji.

facts: Named after Nishida Kitarō, the Kyoto University philosopher who walked here daily to think.
The canal is part of the Lake Biwa Canal, built in the 1890s to bring water and power to Kyoto.
tips: 📿 stamps at the small temples and shrines along the way (Ōtoyo, Hōnen-in).

K8c.name: Ginkaku-ji
K8c.why: The best-known garden of the east side, with an easy walking loop.
K8c.access: North end of the Philosopher's Path, ~5 min uphill.
see: Kannon-den, the 'Silver Pavilion' (outside view).
Ginshadan, the raked 'silver sand sea', and Kōgetsudai, the sand cone.
Moss garden and pond.
Viewpoint on the hill path over the pavilion and the city.

route.enter: Sōmon gate and the tall camellia hedge (Ginkaku-ji-gaki).
walk: One-way loop: sand garden → Hondō → pond → Kannon-den → hill path → viewpoint → down.
route.exit: Same gate; bus stop Ginkakuji-michi ~10 min.

facts: Built from 1482 as the retirement villa of the shogun Ashikaga Yoshimasa; it became a Zen temple (Jishō-ji) after his death.
The Tōgu-dō hall has the Dōjinsai, a 4.5-mat study often called the model for the tea room and the tokonoma alcove.
tips: The loop has steps on the hill section.

K9.name: Shōgunzuka Seiryūden
K9.desc: Quiet viewpoint deck over the city
K9.why: A large wooden deck over all of Kyoto, few visitors.
K9.hours: 9:00–17:00, last entry 16:30; open daily. No autumn night opening announced for 2026.
K9.access: No weekday bus. Taxi from Gion ~15 min, or Tōzai Line to Keage + taxi ~5 min (~¥1,000).
see: The great wooden deck (larger than Kiyomizu's stage).
Seiryūden hall: the Blue Fudō (Ao Fudō), a National Treasure painting (a copy is usually on show; check).
The Shōgunzuka mound.
Maple garden (200+ trees).

route.enter: Car park and gate at the top of Higashiyama Driveway.
walk: Seiryūden hall.
Deck.
Path to the mound and the small viewing platform.
Maple garden.
route.exit: Ask the reception to call a taxi, or take one waiting at the car park.

facts: Legend: in 794 Emperor Kanmu buried a 2.5 m clay statue of a general in armour here, facing the new capital, to guard it. The mound is said to rumble before disasters.
Seiryūden is a branch of Shōren-in temple; the hall was moved here in 2014.
tips: Closes at 17:00 and sunset is ~16:50: sunset light, not sunset itself.

K10.name: Sanjūsangen-dō
K10.why: A unique sight in about an hour, on the way from Kyoto Station to the hotel.
K10.hours: Until 15 Nov 8:30–17:00; from 16 Nov 9:00–16:00. Last entry 30 min before closing. Open daily.
K10.access: From Kyoto Stn: taxi ~10 min, or city bus 100/206/208 to Hakubutsukan Sanjūsangendō-mae (~10 min). Keihan Shichijō Stn 7 min.
see: The 1,000 standing Thousand-armed Kannon in 10 rows.
The large seated Kannon in the centre (National Treasure, by Tankei).
28 guardian deities in front, and Fūjin and Raijin at the ends.
Outside: the 120 m west veranda, where the archery contest was held.

route.enter: Ticket office on the east side; shoes off.
walk: Walk the hall from north to south along the statues.
Out to the garden and the west veranda.
route.exit: South gate (Taiko-no-hei wall); walk ~20 min north-west to the hotel.

facts: Built in 1164 for the retired emperor Go-Shirakawa by Taira no Kiyomori; rebuilt in 1266 after a fire.
The name means 'hall of 33 bays', the spaces between the pillars on the front.
About 124 statues survive from the 1164 temple; the rest were carved in the 1200s.
tips: No photos inside.
📿 stamp at the exit desk.

K11.name: Pontochō dinner
K11.why: Lantern-lit alley of riverside restaurants, 10 min from the night-walk end.
K11.hours: Most restaurants 17:00–22:00/23:00; riverside terraces (yuka) closed in November, indoor dining only.
K11.access: Between Shijō and Sanjō, west bank of the Kamo River; Kyoto-Kawaramachi / Gion-Shijō Stn 3 min.
K11.booking: Most places need a reservation; walk-ins possible at the more casual ones. See Restaurants in claude/reference.md.
see: The 500 m stone-paved alley.
The plover (chidori) lanterns.
Pontochō Kaburenjō theatre at the north end.

route.enter: South end from Shijō-dōri (next to the Kamo River).
walk: North along the alley; the river side has the views.
route.exit: North end at Sanjō; back to the hotel ~25 min walk or taxi.

facts: One of Kyoto's five geiko districts (hanamachi).
The name may come from the Portuguese 'ponto' (point); nobody is sure.
tips: Menus are posted outside: check prices and cover charges first.

K12.name: Northwest route
K12.why: Golden Pavilion and the famous rock garden, but crowded and off our route.
K12.access: Bus 101/205 ~40 min from Kyoto Stn, or taxi ~20–25 min.
see: Kinkaku-ji's gold-leaf pavilion over the pond.
Ryōan-ji rock garden: 15 stones.
Kitano Tenmangū maple garden.
Kamishichiken, the oldest geiko district.

route.enter: Kinkaku-ji at 9:00.
walk: Ryōan-ji (15 min walk) → Kitano Tenmangū → Kamishichiken.
route.exit: Bus or taxi back.

facts: The Golden Pavilion was burned by a young monk in 1950 and rebuilt in 1955; Mishima Yukio's novel 'The Temple of the Golden Pavilion' is based on the fire.
At Ryōan-ji you can never see all 15 stones at once from the veranda.

K13.name: Daitoku-ji
K13.why: Quiet Zen gardens; a good backup, but off our route.
K13.hours: Sub-temples ~9:00–16:30 (not re-checked: not included). Kōtō-in closed since May 2026.
K13.access: Bus 205/206 to Daitokuji-mae, or Karasuma Line Kitaōji + 15 min walk.
see: Daisen-in: dry garden as a river from mountain to sea.
Zuihō-in: modern Zen gardens with a hidden cross.
Ryōgen-in: the smallest rock garden in Japan.

route.enter: Main gate on Kitaōji-dōri.
walk: Open sub-temples are signed at the gate.
route.exit: Same gate.

facts: Daitoku-ji marks its 700th anniversary in 2026.
Sen no Rikyū put his own statue on the Sanmon gate; Hideyoshi had to walk under it, and this was one of the reasons given when he ordered Rikyū's suicide in 1591.

K14.name: Tenryū-ji
K14.desc: Zen pond garden with Arashiyama as backdrop
K14.why: Fills the gap before Ōkōchi opens at 9:00; the garden opens early in late November.
K14.hours: Garden 8:30–17:00 (last entry 16:50); early garden opening from 7:30 on 14–30 Nov 2026 (Walkerplus, tenki.jp), halls from 8:30.
K14.price: Garden ¥500. Halls (+¥300, from 8:30) and Cloud Dragon (+¥500, from 9:00 in 2025) don't fit before Ōkōchi.
K14.access: North gate is on the bamboo path; main gate on the Arashiyama main street.
see: Sōgen-chi pond garden by Musō Soseki, borrowing the Arashiyama hills.
Daihōjō hall: view of the garden from the veranda.
Hattō: the Cloud Dragon ceiling (from 9:00; ⚠️ before our 9:00 Ōkōchi slot).

route.enter: North gate on the bamboo path (ticket booth).
walk: Hyakka-en flower garden down to the pond.
Pond edge, then the Daihōjō veranda (halls from 8:30).
route.exit: North gate back to the bamboo path, up to Ōkōchi Sansō.

facts: Founded in 1339 by the shogun Ashikaga Takauji to honour Emperor Go-Daigo; first of Kyoto's five great Zen temples.
The pond garden is one of the oldest in Japan that still keeps its original form (14th century).
tips: Garden ticket only is enough at 7:30; the halls open at 8:30.

K15.name: Kaiseki dinner
K15.why: The top Kyoto food experience, but the Yoshino stay already includes a multi-course dinner.
K15.hours: Usually one or two seatings from ~17:30–19:00.
K15.booking: Restaurant not chosen yet; book (see Restaurants in claude/reference.md).
see: Seasonal courses: sakizuke, soup, sashimi, grilled, simmered, rice, sweets.
facts: Kaiseki comes from the light meal served at the tea ceremony; the name means 'warm stone', which monks held against the stomach to forget hunger.
tips: Tell the restaurant about allergies when booking.

K16.name: Mishima-tei
K16.why: Kyoto's classic sukiyaki house in a Meiji townhouse; wagyu cooked at the table, a different style from the Kobe teppanyaki.
K16.hours: 11:00–21:00, last entry 19:30; normally closed Wed. ⚠️ Kyoto's tourism site says no closing days in November and December; other listings differ (one says 11:30–22:00).
K16.access: Teramachi-dōri Sanjō-sagaru; Kyoto Shiyakusho-mae Stn 5 min, Keihan Sanjō 8 min; ~20 min walk from the hotel.
K16.booking: Reservation required: kyoto-mishimatei.com or My Concierge Japan (+10% fee).
see: Butcher shop on the ground floor; dining rooms upstairs (2F hall, 3F private rooms).
facts: Opened in 1873, a few years after the Meiji government lifted the old taboo on eating beef.
tips: Last entry 19:30, so it does not fit after the Tue 17 night walk (ends 20:00).

K18.name: Uji
K18.desc: Taihō-an tea ceremony, Byōdō-in, old tea shops
K18.why: Byōdō-in and an authentic short tea ceremony; only worth it combined with Fushimi Inari (K7).
K18.hours: Byōdō-in 8:45–17:30 (last entry 17:15). Taihō-an 10:00–16:00 (last start 15:30), closed the last day of each month.
K18.price: Byōdō-in ¥700 (+¥300 Phoenix Hall interior). Taihō-an usucha booked, ¥3,000 for both.
K18.access: JR Inari 8:33 → Uji 8:50 (¥240); Byōdō-in 10–15 min walk.
K18.booking: BOOKED: Taihō-an Wed 18 11:00, RSV_261118_16 (show the QR at reception).
see: Byōdō-in Phoenix Hall over its pond.
Hōshōkan museum: the original bronze phoenixes and 26 of the 52 Bodhisattvas on clouds.
Omotesandō tea street.
Taihō-an tea ceremony.
Uji Bridge and Tsūen tea shop.

route.enter: JR Uji Stn → Byōdō-in omotesandō (tea shops) → Byōdō-in main gate.
walk: Byōdō-in 9:00–10:00 (Phoenix Hall tour slots every ~20 min from 9:30).
Optional K33 Ujigami (10:10–10:30), across the river.
Taihō-an 10:50 for the 11:00 ceremony.
route.exit: Walk back to JR Uji (~15 min) for the 11:52 train to Nara.

facts: Byōdō-in was a Fujiwara villa turned into a temple in 1052; the Phoenix Hall (1053) is on the 10-yen coin.
Uji tea has been famous since the 1300s; Hideyoshi and the Tokugawa shoguns had Uji tea sent to them in a yearly procession.
tips: Phoenix Hall interior tours are in Japanese; the outside is the main sight.
Matcha shops limit purchases to ~1 per person.

K19.name: Camellia Flower Teahouse, Ninenzaka
K19.why: Backup tea ceremony right on the Higashiyama walk (K1), no extra travel; more lesson-style than Taihō-an.
K19.booking: Book online on the teahouse's own site.
see: A small tatami tea room in an old townhouse.
You whisk your own matcha after the host's demonstration.
facts: The host explains each step in English, so it works well as a first ceremony.
tips: First sessions start after our early walk would be finished: it costs waiting time.

K20.name: Eikan-dō (Zenrin-ji)
K20.why: One of Kyoto's best maple temples, next to Nanzen-ji on the east route; only if we pass by.
K20.hours: 9:00–17:00, reception until 16:00. Autumn treasure exhibition from 11 Nov. Night light-up 20 Nov–6 Dec (after we leave).
K20.price: Daytime ¥1,500 during the autumn exhibition (¥600 otherwise).
K20.access: ~10 min walk north of Nanzen-ji; bus stop Nanzenji-Eikandō-michi 3 min.
K20.booking: No booking; no advance tickets. Long queues in late November.
see: Mikaeri Amida: the Buddha looking back over his shoulder, in the Amida-dō.
Covered 'garyūrō' corridor climbing the hill like a dragon.
Tahōtō pagoda view over the maples and the city.
Hōjō-ike pond.

route.enter: Main gate on Shishigatani-dōri.
walk: Halls (shoes off) → Amida-dō → corridor up → Tahōtō → down to the pond.
route.exit: Main gate; Philosopher's Path south end is 5 min north.

facts: About 3,000 maples.
Legend: in 1082 the monk Eikan was walking around the Amida statue chanting when it stepped down, walked ahead, then looked back and said 'Eikan, you are slow.'
tips: Mid-November colour is early: decide on the day by the queue at the gate.

K21.name: Himeji Castle
K21.why: Japan's best-preserved original castle; Ieyasu gave Himeji to his son-in-law Ikeda Terumasa after Sekigahara.
K21.hours: 9:00–17:00, last entry 16:00. Closed 29–30 Dec. The keep admits ~1,000 people an hour.
K21.price: Included in the tour (non-resident ¥2,500; castle + Kōko-en ¥2,600). Kōko-en alone ¥400.
K21.access: Himeji Stn north exit, 15–20 min walk straight up Ōtemae-dōri (the castle is in view the whole way).
K21.booking: BOOKED: guided tour Sat 14 Nov 10:00, 2.5 h, tickets included (GetYourGuide GYGG45F7WN99). Meet 9:50 at Otemon Gate.
see: Hishi-no-mon gate, the largest gate, with diamond-shaped windows.
Maze of gates and paths: they turn and narrow to slow attackers.
Main keep: six floors inside, steep wooden stairs, the two great pillars.
Nishi-no-maru and the Hyakken corridor (Senhime's rooms).
Okiku's Well and the Ubagaishi stone in the wall.
Kōko-en: nine walled gardens on the lord's west residence site.

route.enter: Otemon Gate (after Sakuramon Bridge), 9:50, guide's 'Himeji Tourism Concierge' sign.
walk: Tour route (guide): Sannomaru → Hishi-no-mon → Nishi-no-maru and Hyakken corridor → main keep → Bizen-maru.
After the tour, walk 5 min west to Kōko-en (12:30–13:20).
route.exit: Kōko-en exit → Ōtemae-dōri → Himeji Stn (~15 min).

facts: The present keep was finished in 1609 by Ikeda Terumasa; it has never been besieged.
It survived the 1945 firebombing of Himeji: a bomb that hit the top floor did not explode (local story).
In 1993 it became one of Japan's first two UNESCO World Heritage sites, with Hōryū-ji.
Eight buildings are National Treasures and 74 are Important Cultural Properties.
tips: Shoes off in the keep and the corridor: socks and a shoe bag (bags are given out).
No big bags inside: lockers at Himeji Stn.
Lunch near the station: Himeji oden (with ginger soy) or anago (conger eel) rice.

K22.name: Engyō-ji, Mt. Shosha
K22.desc: 966 mountain temple, ropeway; Last Samurai filming site
K22.why: Quiet 1,000-year-old temple in the forest after Himeji; skipped for Sanjūsangen-dō and an easier evening.
K22.hours: 8:30–18:00, last ropeway down 17:00 (not re-checked: not included).
K22.price: Entry ¥800, ropeway ¥1,200 return, bus ¥320 each way. Cash.
K22.access: Bus from Himeji Stn ~30 min, ropeway 4 min, then 15 min walk or minibus.
see: Maniden hall on stilts.
Mitsunodō: three great halls around a courtyard.
facts: Founded in 966 by the monk Shōkū.
Scenes of 'The Last Samurai' (2003) were filmed at the Mitsunodō.

K23.name: Samurai Ninja Museum Kyoto
K23.desc: 1 h guided samurai/ninja intro, shuriken, costume photos
K23.why: A fun guided hour with genuine armour pieces near Shijō, but tourist-oriented and overlaps T3/T14.
K23.hours: Daily; start times and prices only in the booking calendar.
K23.access: 109 Horinouechō, Nakagyō-ku, near Shijō; ~15 min from the hotel.
K23.booking: Book online (mai-ko.com); advance booking recommended. kyoto.samurai@maikoya.com.
see: Armour, helmets and swords (genuine historical pieces) with an English guide.
Shuriken throwing.
Samurai costume photos (replicas).
facts: Run by MAIKOYA, which also runs tea-ceremony and kimono experiences.
tips: Pairs with Nishiki Market (K31), 10 min away.

K24.name: Tōfuku-ji
K24.desc: Zen gardens, Tsūten-kyō maple bridge; 5 min from Fushimi Inari
K24.why: A great autumn-colour temple right after Fushimi Inari, but it doesn't fit before the 14:30 Yoshino shuttle.
K24.hours: Autumn 8:30–16:30 (last entry 30 min before; not re-checked: not included).
K24.access: JR / Keihan Tōfukuji Stn, ~10 min walk.
see: Tsūten-kyō covered bridge over a maple valley.
Hōjō gardens by Shigemori Mirei (1939), with the checkerboard moss.
facts: Founded in 1236; its name joins Tōdai-ji and Kōfuku-ji, the two great temples of Nara.

K25.name: Arashiyama Park Observation Deck
K25.why: Short uphill walk to a free view over the Hozu gorge; fits the 8:30–9:00 gap before Ōkōchi opens.
K25.access: Kameyama area of the park, ~10 min uphill from the bamboo path / Tenryū-ji north gate.
see: Hozu River gorge from above; boats and the Sagano train line in the valley.

route.enter: From the end of the bamboo path, into Kameyama park.
walk: Follow signs to the 展望台 (observation deck).
route.exit: Back down to the bamboo path; Ōkōchi Sansō is 5 min.

facts: The Hozu gorge was made navigable in 1606 by the merchant Suminokura Ryōi; his statue stands in the park.
tips: Wet paths after rain.

K26.name: Arashiyama Park Kameyama Area
K26.desc: Quiet park next to the bamboo path
K26.why: Quiet park next to the bamboo path and Tenryū-ji; a calm walk, no ticket.
K26.access: End of the bamboo path, south-west.
see: Maples on the slopes.
Statue of Suminokura Ryōi, the merchant who opened the Hozu River to boats.
Monument with a poem by Zhou Enlai, who visited as a student in 1919.
facts: The park is named after Emperor Kameyama, whose tomb is nearby.
tips: Wild monkeys sometimes come down from Iwatayama: don't show food.

K27.name: Daihikaku Senkō-ji
K27.desc: Hillside temple with a view hall
K27.why: Hillside temple with a view over the gorge, almost no visitors; costs 30–45 min.
K27.hours: ⚠️ Sources differ: 9:00–17:00 (local magazine) or 10:00–16:00 (Sagano tourism page). Either way it doesn't open before our 8:30–9:00 gap.
K27.access: ~20 min walk upstream along the river from Togetsukyō, then ~200 stone steps.
see: Kannon hall on the cliff over the Hozu River.
Wooden statue of Suminokura Ryōi.
The temple bell, which visitors may ring (ask first).
facts: Founded in 1614 by Suminokura Ryōi to pray for the workers who died opening the Hozu River.
tips: Steep steps; not for a tired day.
K27.decision: Optional; probably not, the hours don't fit the gap

K28.name: Iwatayama Monkey Park
K28.desc: Hilltop with wild macaques and a city view
K28.why: ~15–20 min climb to a city view with ~120 monkeys; opens 9:00, so it clashes with Ōkōchi.
K28.hours: 9:00–16:00 (summit until 16:30); closed in heavy rain or snow.
K28.access: Across Togetsukyō bridge, entrance by Ichitani Shrine.
see: Summit area (160 m) with the Kyoto view.
Feeding hut: you are inside, the monkeys outside.
facts: Opened in the 1950s; the staff keep family records of every monkey.
tips: Don't look monkeys in the eye; no food outside the hut.

K29.name: Kawai Kanjirō's House
K29.desc: Potter's wooden home and climbing kiln, 1937
K29.why: Quiet, authentic old house about 15 min walk from the hotel; a calm alternative for the morning.
K29.hours: 10:00–17:00; closed Mondays and during summer and winter breaks.
K29.access: 563 Gojōzaka Kanei-chō, Higashiyama-ku; ~15 min walk east of the hotel.
see: The house Kawai designed himself, with his furniture and pottery.
The noborigama: a climbing kiln with several chambers up the slope.
facts: Kawai Kanjirō (1890–1966) was a leader of the mingei (folk craft) movement with Yanagi Sōetsu and Hamada Shōji.
He turned down the title of Living National Treasure and the Order of Culture.
tips: You may sit on the chairs and touch some objects: ask staff.

K31.name: Nishiki Market
K31.why: Quick food walk close to the hotel.
K31.hours: Shops vary, roughly 9:00/10:00–17:00/18:00; some closed Wed or Sun.
K31.access: Between Teramachi and Takakura, one block north of Shijō; ~15–20 min walk north of the hotel.
see: ~130 shops: pickles, tofu, dashimaki, fish, sweets.
Aritsugu (east end): knife makers since 1560, names engraved on request (hours verify).
Murals of Itō Jakuchū's paintings in the arcade.
Nishiki Tenmangū shrine at the Teramachi end, with its torii going into the buildings.

route.enter: West end at Takakura-dōri.
walk: East along the street; eat at each stall where you buy.
route.exit: East end at Teramachi / Nishiki Tenmangū; the Samurai Ninja Museum is ~10 min.

facts: Fish shops have traded here since at least the early 1600s.
The painter Itō Jakuchū (1716–1800) was born here, the son of a greengrocer.
tips: No eating while walking: stand at the stall.
Many stalls are cash only.

K33.name: Ujigami Shrine
K33.desc: Oldest surviving shrine building in Japan, UNESCO
K33.why: Quick, free stop ~10 min from Byōdō-in, before the tea ceremony.
K33.access: Across the Uji River from Byōdō-in (Asagiri bridge), ~10 min.
see: Honden: three small shrines under one roof, late Heian (~1060).
Haiden hall in the style of an aristocrat's house.
Kirihara spring, the last of Uji's seven famous springs.
facts: Tree-ring dating puts the Honden at about 1060, making it the oldest surviving shrine building in Japan.
tips: 📿 stamp if the office is open.

K34.name: Togetsukyō Bridge
K34.desc: Arashiyama's landmark bridge over the river
K34.why: On the way from Hankyu Arashiyama to the bamboo path, no detour; calm just after sunrise.
K34.access: ~7 min walk from Hankyu Arashiyama Stn; ~10 min walk on to the bamboo path.
see: The Arashiyama hillside behind the bridge.

K35.name: Saga-Toriimoto preserved street
K35.desc: Preserved old street on the road to Atago
K35.why: Your pick: quiet old houses on the way from Giō-ji to Adashino.
see: Machiya houses at the lower end; thatched roofs further up.
K35.decision: Your pick; optional, Sun 15 after Giō-ji

K36.name: Adashino Nenbutsu-ji
K36.desc: 8,000 stone memorials and a small, quiet bamboo path
K36.why: Your pick: the quiet bamboo path at the back of the temple, smaller and steeper than the main grove, with far fewer people.
K36.access: ~5 min walk from Saga-Toriimoto; ~25–30 min walk to Saga-Arashiyama Stn (estimate).
see: The field of about 8,000 stone statues and markers.
The bamboo path at the back, up the small steps.
facts: The stones commemorate people once buried in the Adashino area.
tips: No slack: leave by ~11:40 for the ~12:15 train to Nijō.

K37.name: Ryōan-ji
K37.desc: Zen temple with Japan's most famous rock garden
K37.why: Your pick: the famous 15-stone rock garden. Can get busy, and mid-November is before peak colour.
K37.access: Taxi from Gojō Karasuma ~25–30 min (estimate), or city bus 59 from Shijō Kawaramachi to Ryoanji-mae; Randen Ryoanji Stn ~8 min walk.
see: The rock garden from the Hōjō veranda.
Kyōyō-chi pond walk.
tips: An option for Tue 17 morning, instead of K23.
